text:
kelly: FYI onboarding for tenant 'acme-inc' is intermittently failing. SCIM create calls sometimes get HTTP 409, but the IDP console doesn't show the user. Audit index missing corresponding user.create rows for the window around 2026-03-18T15:12Z. Anyone seen this pattern?

sam: short: 409 could mean duplicate externalId at the IdP while our create aborted locally. paste provisioning logs?

kelly: log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T15:11:58Z INFO provisioning svc: start create externalId=acme-ops-4421
2026-03-18T15:12:00Z ERROR kms-client: Decrypt failed: AccessDenied
2026-03-18T15:12:00Z ERROR provisioning svc: abort create due to kms decrypt error
2026-03-18T15:12:01Z WARN provisioning svc: retrying create (attempt=2)
2026-03-18T15:12:02Z ERROR scim-client: HTTP 409 Conflict {"detail":"User with externalId already exists"}
```

anika: that sequence screams KMS decrypt race: we failed to decrypt our data key, aborted the create (so we never emitted audit.create), but the IdP report says the user exists (maybe previous partial create succeeded). Check key grants/policies.

jonah: did we change the provisioning instance role recently? AccessDenied on Decrypt usually means the principal doesn't have permission on the CMK (key policy vs alias nuance).

kelly: yes we rotated the instance role last night to lock down other permissions. I assumed KMS access carried over.

sam: confirm identity used by the provisioning process with sts get-caller-identity when running as the service principal. Then run aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-id> to see if there's a grant for that role. Grants are commonly missed during rotations.

anika: also remember: granting access to alias does not bypass the CMK's key policy. Key policy must allow that IAM principal or the grant must explicitly reference it.

kelly: ran sts as the service container; it shows the new role ARN. list-grants shows a grant, but it's for the old role ARN. no grant for new role.

jonah: that explains it. On attempted create, Decrypt was denied, provisioning aborted. The IdP probably received the create from a concurrent worker (race) or a partial proceed before our abort, hence 409. Audit pipeline didn't get user.create because our flow didn't publish it.

sam: immediate remediation: either re-create a grant for the new role (preferable) or temporarily roll back the role to the old ARN while we fix grants. When creating a grant, ensure Operations include Decrypt and GenerateDataKey if using envelope encryption.

anika: long-term, I recommend key policy that references a dedicated IAM role for provisioning (less fragile than per-instance grants), and a pre-rotation checklist that updates grants. Also add a smoke test: run aws kms decrypt on a test envelope during role rotation.

kelly: I created a grant with Decrypt+GenerateDataKey for the new role and retried onboarding. The SCIM call now returns 201 for the test user, but we still have missing audit rows for earlier attempts.

jonah: check the provisioning service DLQ for the audit producer or for the provisioning topic; replay entries that didn't make it to the audit index. Do we keep a DLQ for the audit pipeline?

kelly: yes, provisioning->audit producer has a DLQ and it contains the 15:12 items. I'll replay the DLQ for 15:10-15:20 just for acme-inc.

sam: also check CloudTrail for KMS:Decrypt errors to capture which principal errored and which key. That helps proof the timeline in the postmortem.

anika: another note for customer: their IdP is configured to accept transient NameID formats. If provisioning uses externalId linked to NameID, transient NameIDs can change and cause duplicate create attempts. Request they pin NameIDFormat to persistent for provisioning flows.

kelly: noted. I'll reach out to acme and ask them to pin persistent. I'll also add a check in the onboarding handshake that rejects transient NameID for provisioning flows and surfaces a clear error to the customer.

jonah: add runbook items: 1) after any provisioning role rotation, update/create KMS grants and run a decrypt smoke test. 2) monitor for spikes in provisioning service KMS:Decrypt AccessDenied. 3) enable an alert when audit.create events are missing for provisioning success responses.

sam: will file a small RFC to update onboarding docs and automation. Also propose a periodic background job that reconciles IdP user state vs audit index for recent windows to catch these gaps quickly.

infra-bot: started DLQ replay job provisioning-dlq job_id rpl-20260318-01

kelly: replay finished, audit rows for acme restored, no new 409s in the last 40m. closing this thread. thanks :tada:
